 :JUDGMENT:
This claim petition emanates in respect of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner by name Sri Mahesh in the Road Traffic Accident dated 13.08.2023.
2. Succinctly stated the facts germane to the lis involved in this petition are briefly summarized as follows:
That on 13.08.2023 at about 11.00 a.m., when the petitioner was riding his motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-50-EK- 0870 from Yelahanka towards Devanahalli side slowly on left side of the road and when he reached near Doddajala Flyover up ramp, B.B. Road, NH-7, Bengaluru, at that time, respondent's Electric Car bearing Reg.No.KA-03-AK-9095 SCCH 15 3 MVC No.7529/2023 (herein after referred to as the offending vehicle) was driven in a rash and negligent manner with high speed, all of a sudden came and dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner.

As a result,
petitioner fell down from motorcycle and sustained grievous injuries due to the impact of the accident.

3. Immediately, after the accident petitioner was shifted to Life Care hospital, after first aid treatment he was shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma & Orthopaedic, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient.

entities.text: Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma & Orthopaedic
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Hence, the petitioner has claimed compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- with cost and interest at the rate of 12% p.a in the interest of justice and equity.
4. In pursuance of service of notice issued to the Respondents, Respondent No.1 remained absent and he was placed exparte.

The Respondent No.2 has filed written statement submitting as follows:
The respondent No.2 admitted that it has issued policy to the offending vehicle in favour of the respondent No.1.
Without SCCH 15 4 MVC No.7529/2023 prejudice the liability of the respondent No.2 if any is subject to the validity of driving license and terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
The Respondent No.2 in its Objection Statement denied that the accident was caused by rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The driver of the offending vehicle did not have valid and effective driving license as on the date of the accident.
The petition is bad for non joinder of necessary parties.
Hence, on these grounds Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

5. Vide order dated 22.08.2024 the following issues were framed by this Tribunal :-
ISSUES 1) Whether the Petitioner proves that, he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 13.08.2023 at about 11.00 a.m., near Doddajala Fly Mahesh S R vs Blue Smart Mobility Pvt Ltd on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153903512/
2 over up ramp, B.B. Road, NH- 7, Bengaluru City, due to rash and negligent SCCH 15 5 MVC No.7529/2023 driving of the driver of the Electric Car bearing Reg.No.KA-03-AK-9095?

2) Whether the Petitioner is entitled for the compensation as prayed for? If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay?

6. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and examined one witness as PW.2 and relied upon Ex.P.1 to 17 documents.
7. Oral submissions were advanced by Ld. Counsel for parties in this case.

Having perused the records my issue wise findings run as under:-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.3 :
As per the Final Order  for the following :
REASONS 8. Issue No.1:
Before adjudication of the issue with respect to the compensation it is quintessential to adjudicate SCCH 15 6 MVC No.7529/2023 on the issue of negligence.
It is the contention of the petitioner that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Electric Car bearing Reg.No.KA-03- AK-9095/offending vehicle.

9. In this regard the petitioner has got examined himself as PW.1 and in his chief-examination he has deposed that on 13.08.2023 at about 11.00 a.m., he was riding his motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-50-EK-0870 from Yelahanka towards Devanahalli side slowly on left side of the road and when the petitioner reached near Doddajala Flyover up ramp, B.B. Road, NH-7, Bengaluru, at that time, driver of the offending vehicle came from Bengaluru side with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner.
As a result, petitioner fell down from motorcycle and sustained grievous injuries due to the impact of the accident.

10. The petitioner in support of his claim has in addition to describing the course of the accident in line with the facts mentioned in the complaint has relied upon Ex.P1 to 7 SCCH 15 7 MVC No.7529/2023 documents.

Ex.P1 is the FIR registered against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offenses under Sec.279 and 337 of IPC and under Sec.134(a & b) and 187 of MV Act on the basis of the complaint given by one Mahesh on 13.08.2023 hence, there is no delay in lodging the complaint.

Further Ex.P3 is the spot mahazar which discloses the accident spot and on perusal of the spot sketch it discloses that the accident is at the distance of about 8 feet from the edge of the road and width of the road is about 40 feet and the driver of the offending vehicle has dashed the Mahesh S R vs Blue Smart Mobility Pvt Ltd on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153903512/

entities.text: Mahesh S R vs Blue Smart Mobility Pvt Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3 bike of the petitioner at a distance of 8 feet from the edge of the road, which was coming from the same direction, resulting in the accident.
Ex.P4 is the IMV report which discloses the damages sustained to the vehicles and which shows that the front and left side of the two wheeler and front side of the offending vehicle has been damaged.

In this regard it is submitted by the learned counsel for the respondent that as per the damages it indicates that the petitioner himself was negligent and the charge sheet is SCCH 15 8 MVC No.7529/2023 filed against unknown car and there are no documents to show involvement of vehicle in the accident.

However, Ex.P7 is the charge sheet filed after completion of investigation against the driver of the offending vehicle and the contents of the charge sheet discloses that it is offending vehicle which was involved in the accident and when the petitioner was proceeding on its side the offending vehicle came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the bike from the hind side, resulting in the accident.

Ex.P8 is the notice issued under Sec.133 of MV Act which has been replied by owner of the offending vehicle as per Ex.P9 wherein the owner of the offending vehicle has given the details of the driver of the vehicle and other particulars and has not disputed the involvement of the vehicle in the accident.
In addition as far as the damages are concerned damages can also be happen to the vehicle after fall of the vehicle on the road due to the force in which it has fallen.
Hence, the damages on the vehicle itself are not conclusive to prove the manner of the accident.

Hence, SCCH 15 9 MVC No.7529/2023 on the basis of these documents produced by the petitioner it is satisfactorily established that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

11. As far as the manner of the accident is concerned PW.1 is cross-examined by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 and in the cross-examination of PW.1 he has deposed that since he had lost conscious he did not know the number of the vehicle and hence the complaint is given against the unknown vehicle.
However, he knows mode and nature of the vehicle which caused the accident and has furnished those details and submitted further statement to the police mentioning the vehicle number.
He has deposed that the complaint was given in the hospital and denied that in collusion with the owner of the offending vehicle he has filed false complaint.

Except the suggestion that the accident has taken place due to the negligence on the petitioner's side nothing much is elicited in the cross-examination of PW.1 to prove that the accident took place due to the negligence or SCCH 15 10 MVC No.7529/2023 rashness on the part of petitioner.
The petitioner has clearly and categorically deposed about the manner of the accident.
The oral testimony of PW.1 has stood unrebutted and PW1 has withstood the cross-examination of Respondent No.2.
There is no material on record which suggests falsity or untruth in the oral testimony of PW.1 as to the facts and circumstances surrounding cause of the accident.
PW.1 has also denied the suggestion imputing the cause of the accident to be due to his negligence.

The fact that the rider of the offending vehicle has already been charge sheeted for the offences under Sec.279, 337 and 338 of IPC and Sec.134(a & b) r/w Sec.187 of MV Act itself is strong circumstance to support the oral testimony of PW.1.
The certified copies of FIR, charge sheet, IMV report and Spot mahazar also corroborate the oral testimony of PW.1.
In view of medical records there is no dispute regarding the nature of injuries sustained by PW.1 in the above accident.

In view of the said discussion it is satisfactorily established that PW.1 suffered grievous injuries on account of rashness and SCCH 15 11 MVC No.7529/2023 negligence of driver,
driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
Hence, issue No.1 is answered in favour of the petitioner and in the 'Affirmative'.

sentences.text: Issue No.2:
In view of the findings on issue No.1 in favour of petitioner, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
The computation of compensation will have to be decided separately under various heads.
13. MEDICAL OR TREATMENT EXPENSES:
As far as the medical bills are concerned the petitioner has produced Ex.P17 - Prescriptions of Lifecare hospital and also produced Ex.P13 - case sheet of Sanjaygandhi hospital.
Ex.P6 is the wound certificate of Lifecare hospital which discloses that the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries due to the impact of the accident.
Ex.P16 are the medical bills.

As far as the medical bills are concerned in the cross-examination of PW.1 he has deposed that after the accident he was admitted in NRK hospital and he sustained injury to his left hand and was admitted as an inpatient and was admitted in Lifecare hospital SCCH 15 12 MVC No.7529/2023 for almost 2 hours and then went to Sanjaygandhi hospital and some amount is reimbursed in Arogyabhagya scheme.
However, Ex.P16 are pertaining to payments made by cash and nothing much is elicited in the cross-examination of PW.1 to dispute the authenticity of the said bills.
Hence petitioner is entitled to an amount of Rs.16,337/- under this head.
14. PAIN AND SUFFERING:

As per the medical documents the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries and Ex.P6 discloses that the petitioner has sustained distal radius bone fracture on left hand and it is stated in the petition that injuries sustained and physical impairment has caused unbearable pain and petitioner cannot do any work as prior to the accident.

It is not possible to ascertain quantum of compensation admissible to petitioner for the shock, pain and sufferings etc.,
which he actually suffered due to the accidental injuries.

Keeping in view the trauma and nature of the injuries suffered by the petitioner and duration of the treatment taken by him etc., an amount of Rs.30,000/- is SCCH 15 13 MVC No.7529/2023 awarded to him towards pain and sufferings.

Thus,
he is awarded an amount of Rs.30,000/- under this head.
15. LOSS OF ACTUAL EARNINGS:
In his evidence PW.1 has submitted he was aged about 30 years and he was working as an Electrician and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
However in his cross-examination he has deposed that he has not produced any documents to prove his avocation and income.

In the absence of any material as to the monthly earnings of the petitioner it would be proper to assume the monthly earnings of the petitioner as per the notional income as on the date of the accident.
As per the minimum wages chart the income for the said avocation for the relevant period is ranging between 14,000 to 16,000/- and hence the notional income is taken as Rs.16,000/- p.m.

Taking into consideration that the petitioner due to the injuries he might not have been in a position to work for at least 3 months hence, as such the petitioner is entitled to an amount of Rs.16,000 X 3 = 48,000/- under this head.
SCCH 15 14 MVC No.7529/2023 16.
LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS DUE TO DISABILITY:

The petitioner has claimed in his affidavit he has permanent disability and as per the evidence of PW.2 his impairment is not progressive and will not improve in future and hence it is submitted by the petitioner that he cannot pursue his work as before Mahesh S R vs Blue Smart Mobility Pvt Ltd on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153903512/

In support of the same, PW.2 - Orthopaedic Surgeon is examined and he has deposed that the petitioner has sustained left distal and he underwent surgery in form ORIF with plate and screws and has mild swelling of forearm and wrist and pain and tenderness over the fracture site and wrist joint and range of movements of elbow wrist restricted and fracture is united with implant in situ and he has difficulty in lifting weight and over head abduction and stated that the petitioner has 41%
disability to the upper limb and 14% disability to the whole body.
PW.2 is cross

- examined by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 and in his cross- examination he has deposed that the fracture has united and SCCH 15 15 MVC No.7529/2023 admitted that the right hand is used more when compared to left hand and advised physiotheraphy and removal of implant.
PW.2 has denied that he has assessed disability on higher side.
The monthly income of the petitioner is already assessed at Rs.16,000/- at the relevant time.
As far as, age of the petitioner at the time of the accident is concerned on perusal of the petitioner's Aadhaar card Ex.P11 the date of birth of the petitioner is 10.08.1993.
Going by the same, the age of petitioner as on date of accident i.e., 13.08.2023 was around 30 years.

Therefore, in view of the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma and others Vs. Delhi Corporation and another (2009) 6 SCC 121, which has also been upheld by the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the judgment dated 31.10.2017 given in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors.

The loss of future SCCH 15 16 MVC No.7529/2023 earnings of petitioner due to above injury and permanent physical disability comes to Rs.4,56,960/- (Rs.16,000/-
X 12 X 17 X 14%) and the same is awarded to him as compensation under this head.
17. Loss of Amenities:

In view of the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, the extent of permanent physical disability and the extended period of medical treatment, the petitioner is granted a sum of Rs.20,000/- under this head.

18. Attendant's charges, Special diet and Conveyance:
The facts show that physical condition of the petitioner is such that he might have taken the help of an attendant.
Further, he would be requiring conveyance for movement.
His avocation has been hit due to his disablement.
He might have spent considerable amount towards special diet during his treatment.
Therefore, petitioner is granted Rs.20,000/- under this head.

20. TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :

21. Regarding rate of interest: As far as the rate of interest is concerned the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in SHRIRAM GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. RAJASTAN VS. SMT.

Hence the rate of interest is set at 6% per annum in this case.

sentences.text: Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
There is no dispute about the validity of the Policy at the time of the accident.
Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the insurer is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.1 and has to pay compensation amount to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
23. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on Issues No. 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondent No.1 and 2 U/S 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The Petitioner is entitled for  Compensation of 6,11,297/- along with  SCCH 15 20 MVC No.7529/2023 interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
Out of the compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner, 75% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be released to the Petitioner by way of E-payment and after proper identification.
The remaining 25% award amount shall be deposited as F.D. in the name of the Petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of three years.
The Advocate fee is fixed at 1,000/-.
Draw Award accordingly.
